Test Case Description: Verify that the agent can successfully parse and understand functional requirements and acceptance criteria from a valid requirements document.
Preconditions: Agent is initialized and a valid markdown requirement file is uploaded.
Test Steps: 1. Upload/Provide standard business requirement document containing user stories and acceptance criteria.\n2. Execute the test case generation command.
Test Data: markdown file containing a user story with acceptance criteria
Expected Result: Agent successfully parses the requirements and proceeds to generate test cases without errors.

Test Case Description: Verify that when a requirement is ambiguous, the agent makes reasonable assumptions and lists them separately.
Preconditions: Agent is initialized and a requirements document with ambiguous fields is provided.
Test Steps: 1. Provide requirement document containing ambiguous statements (e.g. "User should login fast").\n2. Execute the test case generation command.
Test Data: Requirement text: "The login page should load quickly and user profile must load safely."
Expected Result: Agent generates test cases and clearly lists the assumptions made about "quickly" (e.g. <2s) and "safely" (e.g. via HTTPS) in a separate section.

Test Scenario: Generate all requested test case types
Test Case Description: Verify that the agent generates positive, negative, edge, boundary, validation, error handling, UI, API, security, and accessibility test cases when applicable.
Preconditions: Agent is provided with a comprehensive specification containing both UI and API requirements.
Test Steps: 1. Input requirement document containing both UI components and API endpoints.\n2. Check the types of test cases generated.
Test Data: Specification containing form inputs, login UI, and an authentication API endpoint
Expected Result: Generated test cases include all 10 requested categories (Positive, Negative, Edge, Boundary, Validation, Error Handling, UI, API, Security, Accessibility) as applicable.

Test Case Description: Verify that the generated test suite contains no duplicate test cases across all generated categories.
Preconditions: Agent is provided with simple requirements.
Test Steps: 1. Provide a requirement document.\n2. Generate the test suite.\n3. Analyze the output for duplicate Test Scenarios or Steps.
Test Data: Simple requirement: "User can reset password by email"
Expected Result: All generated test cases are unique in scenario, steps, and validation coverage; no duplicate entries exist in the output list.

Test Case Description: Verify that the final output matches the exact 13 columns specified in the requirements.
Preconditions: Agent is ready to generate test cases.
Test Steps: 1. Input a requirement snippet.\n2. Run the generator.\n3. Verify the columns in the output header.
Expected Result: The output contains exactly 13 columns in this order: Test Case ID, Requirement ID, Module, Test Scenario, Test Case Description, Preconditions, Test Steps, Test Data, Expected Result, Test Type, Priority, Severity, Automation Candidate (Yes/No)

Test Scenario: Strict CSV escaping with double quotes
Test Case Description: Verify that fields containing commas or newlines are properly enclosed in standard double quotes `"` to prevent parsing issues.
Preconditions: Agent is ready to output CSV.
Test Steps: 1. Trigger test case generation.\n2. Examine the raw output string for steps containing commas or newlines.
Expected Result: Fields with commas (e.g., 'username: testuser, password: Password123') and multiline steps are correctly wrapped in double quotes.

Test Scenario: Boundary and Equivalence Partitioning for numerical input
Test Case Description: Verify that numerical inputs are tested using boundary values (Min, Max, Min-1, Max+1) and equivalence partitions.
Preconditions: Requirement specifies a numeric range constraint.
Test Steps: 1. Input a requirement with a range validation (e.g., Age must be between 18 and 60).\n2. Generate test cases.
Test Data: Requirement: "Age input field accepts values from 18 to 60"
Expected Result: Test cases are generated with specific test data: 17 (Negative/Boundary), 18 (Positive/Boundary), 40 (Positive/Equivalence), 60 (Positive/Boundary), and 61 (Negative/Boundary).

Test Case Description: Verify that text inputs are tested with empty, null, and special character strings.
Preconditions: Requirement specifies a text input field.
Test Steps: 1. Input a requirement for a text field (e.g., Search bar).\n2. Generate test cases.
Test Data: Requirement: "Search field allows users to search products by name"
Expected Result: Test cases are generated targeting empty search, null search, and searching with special characters like `@#$%^*()`.

Test Case Description: Verify that session timeout scenarios are generated for features requiring stateful sessions.
Preconditions: Requirement involves stateful authenticated user sessions.
Test Steps: 1. Input a requirement involving user session or cart preservation.\n2. Generate test cases.
Test Data: Requirement: "User dashboard shows personal details when logged in"
Expected Result: Test cases are generated to verify behavior when the session times out while viewing dashboard or performing actions.

Test Case Description: Verify that authorization/role-based test cases are generated if multiple roles are mentioned.
Preconditions: Requirement mentions multiple user roles with different access rights.
Test Steps: 1. Input a requirement with roles (e.g., Admin and Viewer).\n2. Generate test cases.
Test Data: Requirement: "Admin can delete posts, Viewer can only read posts"
Expected Result: Test cases are generated to verify that Admin can delete, Viewer cannot delete, and unauthorized access is blocked.

Test Case Description: Verify that API test cases validate HTTP status codes like 200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500 as applicable.
Test Steps: 1. Input a requirement describing an authentication or data retrieval API.\n2. Generate test cases.
Expected Result: Test cases are generated to validate response status 200 (Success), 401 (Unauthorized), and 404 (Not Found).

Test Case Description: Verify that test cases include database assertions/validation steps where data persistence is involved.
Preconditions: Requirement involves writing, updating, or deleting database records.
Test Steps: 1. Input a requirement where a resource is created (e.g., registration).\n2. Generate test cases.
Test Data: Requirement: "User registration stores email and phone in database"
Expected Result: Test cases include steps or preconditions suggesting validation of the database state to ensure the correct record is inserted.

Test Scenario: Assign High Priority to critical business flows
Test Case Description: Verify that high priority is assigned only to critical business paths like payment, authentication, or primary user registration.
Test Steps: 1. Input requirements containing both core checkout and cosmetic styling elements.\n2. Verify the assigned priorities.
Expected Result: Checkout flow cases are marked 'High', styling validations are marked 'Low'.

Test Scenario: Assign Severity based on business impact
Test Case Description: Verify that severities are correctly classified as Critical, Major, or Minor depending on the potential business impact.
Test Steps: 1. Check the severity classification in the output.\n2. Confirm that data loss/crash is Critical, flow block is Major, alignment is Minor.
Expected Result: Test cases representing data loss or login block are assigned 'Critical', validation errors are 'Major', UI spacing issues are 'Minor'.

Test Scenario: Output ONLY the CSV/Table without explanations
Test Case Description: Verify that the agent outputs only the CSV/table, without conversational preambles or post-generation explanations unless explicitly asked.
Test Steps: 1. Provide requirements and execute generator.\n2. Check the raw response content.
Expected Result: The response starts directly with the column header row and contains only the CSV data rows, with no additional conversational text.
